title: Thresholded batching config conditional-apply with staged ops gates
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: Implement a conservative, auditable mechanism to apply batching and caching recommendations derived from Optimize so that the system can conditionally adopt cost-saving configs while minimizing user-visible regressions. We will introduce a 'thresholded conditional-apply' flow: recommendations are first dry-run scored against traffic samples, then promoted through a sequence of ops gates (simulation, limited canary, regional expand, full apply) when metrics satisfy policy thresholds. This ticket covers server-side orchestration, control-plane approval lattice, observability hooks, and a rollback choreography that can pause or revert at any stage.
acceptance_criteria: Control plane can accept a suggested batching/caching config and mark it as 'candidate'
Simulation runner produces token-level cost and quality delta estimates from historical traffic samples within 5 minutes
Canary rollout applies candidate configs to a selectable small shard (1-5% traffic) and enforces SLO/QA thresholds
Ops gate evaluation automates promotion only when all configured metrics meet threshold; otherwise it pauses and notifies reviewers
Config apply includes an automated, observable rollback window and a manual 'force-apply' override guarded by a two-person approval
End-to-end e2e smoke test demonstrates a candidate config moving from candidate -> simulate -> canary -> regional -> full in a staging org and logs all decisions
Runbook updated with step-by-step operator commands and links to dashboards and playbooks
design_notes: Key trade-offs: aggressive auto-adoption reduces unit cost faster but increases risk of quality regressions; conservative staged gating increases operator overhead. We chose a middle path: require an initial simulated pass + low-volume canary with automated metric checks, but allow ops to define stricter policies per-customer tier. Implementation will reuse the existing rollout engine but extend it with 'simulation tasks' that replay requests against candidate config using KV cache snapshots. We will avoid model changes in this ticket; only batching/caching/dispatcher knob changes.
rollout_plan: Step 0: Backend: store candidate configs and a simple state machine (candidate, simulated, canary, regional, full, paused, reverted)
Step 1: Simulation: batch-run sampled requests in a simulator to estimate cost delta and top-10 request latencies (bounded by 5m timeout)
Step 2: Canary: apply config to 1% traffic (configurable) with traffic-weighting; monitor metrics for 30m
Step 3: Regional expansion: increase to 10-20% per-region with 1h observation windows
Step 4: Full apply: expand globally if regional windows pass; persist config as default and emit audit record
Step 5: Observability: wire cost, latency, failure-rate, token-reuse, and output-drift signals to ops dashboard
canary_policy: Canary buckets are selected by hashing customer_id (or request_id) into fixed shards to ensure deterministic routing. Default canary size is 1%. Promotion requires: latency p95 change <= 5% absolute or <= 150ms, error-rate increase <= 0.1 percentage points, output-drift A/B score <= 0.02; cost reduction must be > 3% to promote automatically. Policies are configurable per org-level policy and can be tightened for enterprise customers.
rollback_plan: Automatic pause if any metric breaches threshold during canary or regional windows
Automatic revert to previous config if severe breach (error-rate delta > 0.5 pp or p95 increase > 300ms)
Manual revert: ops run `rctl config rollback <candidate-id>` which triggers immediate traffic reweighting back and marks candidate as reverted
Forensic capture: on pause/revert, capture 1 hour of traces + sample outputs for triage
Postmortem: owner to open a short incident note and flag for follow-up improvements
